channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Large-scale potato cultivation project launched in Kashkadarya region
item.description: A major project to ensure food security and cultivate quality seed potatoes has begun in Nishan district, Kashkadarya region. The initiative involves planting 400 hectares of elite Dutch seed potatoes. The project aims to enhance food security and supply the domestic market with quality potatoes.

item.title: Uzbekistan Amends Law on Arbitration Courts, Restricting State Involvement
item.description: Uzbekistan has amended its law on arbitration courts, with the changes taking effect on July 24. State bodies, state-owned enterprises, and civil self-governance bodies can no longer establish arbitration courts or be parties to arbitration agreements. Disputes concerning land, property rights, and budget funds will now be handled by state courts.

item.title: Uzbekistan Prioritizes Quality Education, Investing Heavily in Sector
item.description: Uzbekistan has made quality education a state policy priority, focusing on improving educational standards, teacher status, and infrastructure. In Tashkent region alone, education funding increased 6.2 times to 31.5 trillion soums over ten years. Preschool enrollment rose from 27.2% to 73.9%, and new school year saw increased first-grade admissions.

item.title: Two killed in Surxondaryo after car collides with train at unguarded crossing
item.description: Two women died and two others were injured when a Gentra car collided with a train at an unguarded railway crossing in Denov district, Surxondaryo region. The accident occurred due to the driver's inattention, according to authorities. An investigation is underway.

item.title: Prosecutors seek nine-year sentences in 'Letter of 75' appeal case
item.description: Prosecutors are seeking nine-year prison sentences for all defendants in the 'Letter of 75' case appeal at the Bishkek City Court. This follows a previous verdict where defendants were found guilty of attempting to violently seize power and received four-year sentences with probation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Considers Allowing Residents to Keep Homes Near Issyk-Kul Shoreline
item.description: A bill in Kyrgyzstan's parliament proposes amending rules for houses built within 500 meters of Issyk-Kul's shore. The amendment would allow existing individual homes, built before current restrictions took effect in 2004, to remain if owners have valid land documents. This aims to resolve legal uncertainties for property owners.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Expedited Trademark Registration Process
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering a bill to speed up the registration of trademarks and geographical indications. A key change is introducing accelerated examination, allowing applicants to request faster processing for a fee. The bill also aims to digitize the registration system and enhance flexibility in administrative procedures.

item.title: Uzbek President Meets with World Customs Organization Secretary General
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with the Secretary General of the World Customs Organization. They discussed expanding practical cooperation in improving customs administration, strengthening customs authorities' capacity, and combating offenses.

item.title: Nepal Mourns Over 1,300 Victims of Recent Floods and Landslides
item.description: Nepal is observing a day of mourning for over 1,300 victims of recent floods and landslides in the Bhote Kosi river. The disaster destroyed homes, disrupted infrastructure, and left thousands homeless. Kyrgyzstan confirmed no citizens were among the casualties.

item.title: Tursunzade Farmers Supply Over 70,000 Tons of Agricultural Products to Tajikistan
item.description: Farmers in Tursunzade have supplied over 70,565 tons of agricultural products to markets across Tajikistan, including potatoes, onions, cabbage, tomatoes, and cucumbers. High yields are attributed to modern farming technologies and efficient land use.

item.title: Uzbekistan appoints ambassador to Syria
item.description: Ayubkhon Yunusov, who also serves as Uzbekistan's ambassador to Kuwait and Iraq, has been appointed as the country's ambassador to Syria. This appointment expands diplomatic representation in the region.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Tax Service to Integrate AI with International Expert Assistance
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's State Tax Service (STS) met with Sign, a digital infrastructure developer, to discuss integrating artificial intelligence into tax administration. The collaboration aims to modernize digital infrastructure, enhance analytical systems, and develop domestic IT capabilities through specialist training.

item.title: Tajikistan Celebrates 35th Independence Anniversary in Baku
item.description: A ceremony marking Tajikistan's 35th Independence Day was held in Baku, Azerbaijan, initiated by the Tajik Embassy. The event was attended by Azerbaijani officials, diplomats, and community members. The Tajik Ambassador highlighted the country's achievements, while Azerbaijan's Minister of Digital Development praised bilateral cooperation.

item.title: Uzbekistan Among Countries Selling Gold in July
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank sold one ton of gold in July, according to reports. This occurred as global central banks collectively purchased 23 tons, with China being the largest buyer. Russia also sold gold, while Poland increased its reserves. Despite July's sales, global central banks have increased gold reserves since the start of the year.

item.title: Astana to Host AI & Digital Bridge 2026 Forum on Artificial Intelligence
item.description: Astana will host the AI & Digital Bridge 2026 forum from October 1-3, focusing on artificial intelligence's impact on markets and business. The event aims to connect global BigTech representatives, investors, and partners. Kazakhstan has declared 2026 the Year of Digitalization and Artificial Intelligence, underscoring the forum's strategic importance.

item.title: Uzbek President Meets with Chinese Communist Party Delegation
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev held a meeting with a delegation led by Liu Haixin, head of the International Liaison Department of the CPC Central Committee. Discussions focused on further expanding multifaceted cooperation and practical partnerships between Uzbekistan and China.

item.title: Polat Bobojonov Appointed First Deputy Chairman of Uzbekistan Mahallas Association
item.description: Polat Bobojonov has been appointed the first deputy chairman of the Uzbekistan Mahallas Association. This follows his dismissal from the position of deputy advisor to the president on personnel matters, a role and department that have also been abolished.

item.title: Tajikistan, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan Inspect Disarmament Compliance in China
item.description: Military personnel from Tajikistan, Russia, Kazakhstan, and Kyrgyzstan conducted a disarmament inspection in China's Heilongjiang province on September 7, 2026. The inspection verified compliance with existing agreements on troop numbers and locations with the Chinese People's Liberation Army's 338th missile brigade.

item.title: Farg'ona Governorate and Afghanistan's Kam Air Discuss Establishing New International Airline
item.description: The Farg'ona Governorate and Afghanistan's Kam Air are discussing the establishment of a new international airline. Discussions followed a July visit to Afghanistan where agreements on trade, economic, and investment cooperation were made. Details on launch dates and investment volumes are not yet clarified.

item.title: Number of emigrants from Uzbekistan decreased in first half of 2026
item.description: The number of citizens emigrating from Uzbekistan has decreased. Data for the first half of 2026 indicates the primary destination countries for those who did leave. Further details are available via the provided link.

item.title: CIS intelligence chiefs discuss cooperation in reconnaissance
item.description: Heads of security and intelligence services from CIS countries met in St. Petersburg on September 4, 2026, to discuss intelligence cooperation. Russian President Putin emphasized its importance for sovereignty and security amid geopolitical instability. Participants confirmed commitment to strengthening intelligence collaboration.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Labor Minister Kanat Sagynbaev Dismissed; Almaz Imangaziev Appointed Acting Minister
item.description: Kanat Sagynbaev has been dismissed as Kyrgyzstan's Minister of Labor, Social Security, and Migration. Almaz Imangaziev has been appointed as the acting minister. Imangaziev, a professional diplomat, previously served as Deputy Foreign Minister.

item.title: Tender Announced for Bridge Reconstruction Over Aravan-Ak-Buura Canal in Osh
item.description: Osh city has announced a tender for the reconstruction of a bridge over the Aravan-Ak-Buura canal. The project, managed by 'Osh City Roads' Municipal Enterprise, has a budget of 37.4 million soms. The reconstruction involves demolishing existing structures and building a new reinforced concrete bridge.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan proposes prison for intentional damage to border fences
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has submitted a bill proposing criminal liability for intentionally damaging state border infrastructure. The draft law suggests two to five years in prison for damaging engineering structures and barriers, citing a lack of specific provisions and the risk of unauthorized crossings. Over 320 km of barriers are installed on the Kyrgyz-Tajik border.

item.title: Iran warns US of harsher response amid renewed military tensions
item.description: Iran's leadership has warned the United States of a more painful response as military confrontations between Tehran and Washington intensify. Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf urged the US to properly assess the situation. The warning comes amid renewed military tensions between the two countries.

item.title: Almaz Imangaziev Appointed Acting Labor Minister of Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Kanat Sagynbaev has been dismissed as Kyrgyzstan's Minister of Labor, Social Security, and Migration. Almaz Imangaziev, previously Deputy Foreign Minister, is now acting head of the ministry. His appointment requires approval from the Zhogorku Kenesh. Imangaziev is a career diplomat with a PhD in political science.

item.title: Gazprom Increases Gas Exports to Central Asia by 70 Percent
item.description: Gazprom has increased its gas exports to Central Asia by 70 percent since the beginning of 2026, according to company head Alexey Miller. Deliveries to Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, and Kyrgyzstan are nearing this growth mark. Kyrgyzstan requires nearly half a billion cubic meters of gas annually.

item.title: G'ofurjon Mirzayev appointed Deputy Prime Minister and Chairman of Mahalla Association
item.description: G'ofurjon Mirzayev has been appointed Deputy Prime Minister and Chairman of the Association of Mahallas of Uzbekistan. His candidacy was approved by deputies of the Legislative Chamber of the Oliy Majlis. Mirzayev replaces Kahramon Kurbonov, who held the position since January 17, 2024.

item.title: Gazprom boosts Central Asian gas exports by 70 percent
item.description: Gazprom CEO Alexey Miller announced a 70 percent increase in gas exports to Central Asia since the start of 2026. Supplies to Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, and Kyrgyzstan have approached this mark. Long-term agreements are in place through 2040 for Kyrgyzstan's energy facilities.

item.title: New oil processing line construction begins in Jayhun district
item.description: Construction of a new oil processing line with a capacity of 50,000 tons of petroleum products per year has commenced in the Jayhun district. The Ministry of Energy and Water Resources of Tajikistan reported that the new line will enable the production of diesel fuel and gasoline, expanding the product range beyond bitumen.

item.title: New powers for traffic police and public order units in Uzbekistan
item.description: Uzbekistan is reallocating functions between internal affairs units to enhance public safety. From November 1, 2026, patrol units will respond to crimes and incidents via the '112' system. Patrol units will also gain new responsibilities for traffic safety, including managing congestion in busy areas.

item.title: Uzbek Citizen Sentenced to Two Years for Fighting in Ukraine
item.description: An Uzbek citizen, F.A., who fought for Russia in the Ukraine conflict, has been sentenced to two years in prison in Namangan, Uzbekistan. He was recruited while serving a drug sentence in Russia and participated in combat operations before being injured by a drone strike. He later returned to Uzbekistan and obtained citizenship.

item.title: Uzbek Preventive Police Officers Granted Authority to Issue Fines for Traffic Violations
item.description: Preventive police officers in Uzbekistan have been granted new powers to issue administrative fines for four types of traffic violations on neighborhood streets. This is part of a presidential decree aimed at improving public safety and community engagement. Officers can now also issue warnings for minor offenses.

item.title: Man Arrested for Assault and Threatening to Kill a Cafeteria Worker in Tajikistan
item.description: Authorities in Tajikistan have arrested a man, Nurmurodzoda Zakhriddin, for assaulting and threatening to kill a cafeteria worker in Zafarabad district. The incident occurred on August 19, 2026, when the intoxicated man reportedly argued with and physically attacked the employee, using a cord to threaten her life.

item.title: Ayubkhon Yunusov Becomes Uzbekistan's First Ambassador to Syria
item.description: Ayubkhon Yunusov presented his credentials as Uzbekistan's first ambassador to Syria to Foreign Minister Asad Hasan ash-Shayboni. The meeting focused on strengthening bilateral ties, including establishing a joint trade and economic committee and political consultations. Both sides expressed readiness for further cooperation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Export Berries and Fruits to China Following Phytosanitary Protocol Signing
item.description: Kyrgyzstan will export berries and fruits, including raspberries, blackberries, and currants, to China. A phytosanitary protocol was signed within the Shanghai Cooperation Organization framework, expanding export opportunities beyond traditional EAEU markets and potentially boosting domestic berry cultivation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan School Enrollment: One Week Left for First Grade Registration
item.description: Approximately 143,300 children have been enrolled in first grade in Kyrgyzstan's schools, with Bishkek registering 25,400. Osh has enrolled 10,600 children. Electronic registration began April 1, and parents must submit medical certificates for admitted students. The academic year starts September 15.

item.title: US envoys discuss war end conditions with Zelensky in Kyiv
item.description: US special envoy Stephen Wittekoff and advisor Jared Kushner met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in Kyiv to discuss potential conditions for ending the war. They also discussed short-term Western support and security guarantees for Ukraine. Zelensky indicated the war might continue through winter, requesting winter aid.
